overview: ANZ Group Holdings is one of Australia's "Big Four" banks and the number-one ranked bank in New Zealand, providing retail, commercial and institutional banking across Australia, New Zealand, the Pacific and Asia. Since the July 2024 acquisition of Suncorp Bank, ANZ is Australia's third-largest home lender, and the group is mid-way through a large-scale technology, culture and risk-management reset under new CEO Nuno Matos (appointed May 2025) following an APRA court enforceable undertaking. ANZ.NZ is the NZX foreign-exempt listing of the same ASX-primary-listed entity (reports in AUD, fiscal year end 30 September).

business_model.summary: ANZ earns the large majority of revenue from net interest income on loans (home loans, business/commercial lending, institutional lending) funded by customer deposits and wholesale funding, supplemented by fee, trading (Markets) and transaction banking income. Revenue is broadly recurring/spread-based (net interest margin on a ~$1.16 trillion average interest-earning asset base) rather than transactional, though the Institutional Markets business contributes more volatile trading income.

revenue_streams.name: Net interest income (Retail/Commercial/Institutional lending & deposits)
revenue_streams.trend: growing (Suncorp Bank consolidation, +12% FY2025) but margin under pressure

business_model.customer_type: Mix of B2C retail/mass-market (Australia Retail, Suncorp Bank, NZ Personal), B2B SME/commercial (Australia Commercial, NZ Business/Agribusiness), and large corporate/institutional/government clients globally (Institutional division - Transaction Banking, Corporate Finance, Markets)
business_model.geographic_mix: Cash profit by geography (FY2025): Australia ~$2,933m, New Zealand ~$2,158m, Rest of World (Asia, Pacific, Europe, Americas) ~$840m; segments span Australia Retail, Australia Commercial, Suncorp Bank, Institutional, New Zealand, and Pacific, plus Group Centre

competitive_position.market_position: Third/fourth-largest of Australia's Big Four by home lending (now #3 post-Suncorp Bank acquisition, ~$2.2 trillion combined Big Four home loan market); historically #1 ranked bank in New Zealand by market share, though ANZ NZ's home-loan share slipped to ~30% in 2025 as Kiwibank and ASB gained share; a leading Institutional/corporate bank across Australia, NZ and Asia with a long-standing Asian and European network (e.g. 40-year Frankfurt presence)

moat_factors.description: Big Four Australian banks plus dominant NZ players control the vast majority of banking assets/deposits in a regulated, high-barrier-to-entry duopoly-like market; ANZ now #3 in Australian home loans post-Suncorp
APRA/RBNZ prudential licensing, capital and compliance requirements make new bank entry difficult, protecting incumbents despite intense internal competition
Differentiated pan-Asian and cross-border institutional franchise (Transaction Banking, trade, Markets) that smaller domestic peers cannot easily replicate
Large, sticky customer deposit base (~$770B) provides low-cost funding relative to wholesale markets
Historically strong brand, but repeated regulatory/conduct failures (bond trading scandal, ASIC penalties, APRA CEU) have damaged trust and given challengers/neobanks an opening

weaknesses: Weakest recent non-financial risk management track record among the Big Four, culminating in an APRA court enforceable undertaking and increased capital add-on
Losing NZ home-loan market share to Kiwibank and ASB through 2025
Elevated cost-to-income ratio (58.2% FY2025 cash) versus historical run-rate, inflated by Suncorp integration, restructuring and remediation costs
Execution risk from simultaneous CEO transition, Suncorp Bank integration/migration, ANZ Plus rollout and NFR remediation
Markets/trading income volatility can swing other operating income significantly period to period

growth_drivers: Suncorp Bank integration - migrating ~1.3 million Suncorp customers onto ANZ's platform by June 2027 (34% complete as of March 2026), targeting ~$500m p.a. in run-rate synergies
Accelerated ANZ Plus digital platform rollout to all ~8 million retail customers by September 2027 (three years earlier than original plan), with ANZ Plus already >45% of new retail product sales
Cost/productivity program - FY2026 cost reduction guidance upgraded to ~5% below FY2025 (from an original ~3% target), with FY2026 productivity savings tracking to ~$875m (up from $800m prior target)

New CEO Nuno Matos's 2030 strategy reset ("Customer first, Simplicity, Resilience, Delivering value") and single customer front-end initiative to unify Australia Retail, Commercial and Suncorp onto common technology
Institutional franchise leverage of Asia trade/investment flows amid supply-chain diversification and geopolitical realignment (transaction banking, trade finance)
Capital normalization and return of surplus capital via buybacks/dividends once CET1 build and regulatory remediation are further advanced

business.description: ANZ NZ home-loan share fell to ~30% in 2025 as Kiwibank and ASB took share; increasing NZ competitive intensity and Commerce Commission-driven reforms (open banking) could further pressure NZ margins/share
Accelerated migration timeline (brought forward to June 2027) increases near-term execution and cost risk if delivery slips or customer attrition occurs during transition
Institutional Markets other operating income fell materially in FY2025 (down ~20%) on lower trading gains across Rates, Credit and Commodities; contributes earnings volatility
Gross impaired assets rose ~50% and credit impairment charges increased in FY2025/H1-2026, signalling early-stage deterioration from a benign base

financial.description: NIM (cash) fell to 1.54% in FY2025 from 1.57%, and to 1.53% in H1-2026, driven by deposit/asset pricing competition and wholesale funding costs
APRA's increased operational risk capital add-on (now $1 billion, up from $750m) permanently ties up capital that could otherwise support growth or shareholder returns
H1-2026 payout ratio ~68.5% (cash ~66.2%) is elevated versus historical levels; ROTE (cash 11.6% H1-2026) needs to sustain to support current dividend and any resumed buybacks
Reported earnings affected by AUD/NZD and AUD/USD movements via economic hedging and NZ segment translation

regulatory.risk: APRA Court Enforceable Undertaking / Root Cause Remediation Plan
regulatory.description: April 2025 CEU with APRA over non-financial risk management and risk culture failures; capital add-on raised to $1 billion; multi-year PACT remediation program must be delivered to APRA's satisfaction or further sanctions/capital penalties could follow

September 2025 ASIC settlement and Federal Court orders totalling ~$250 million in penalties across Markets and Retail conduct matters (including 2023 bond-trading misreporting); reputational damage and risk of further legacy conduct issues surfacing

regulatory.risk: NZ Commerce Commission market study follow-through
regulatory.description: ANZ is implementing Commerce Commission recommendations (open banking acceleration) from the NZ personal banking competition study, which could structurally erode NZ margins/market power over time

regulatory.risk: Bank levies and prudential capital changes
regulatory.description: Ongoing major bank levy (~$451m FY2025) and potential future APRA/RBNZ capital rule changes affecting required capital ratios

macro.description: Gradual/sporadic rate cuts across Australia, NZ and other markets affect margin and credit demand; NZ industry revenue forecast to fall as rates decline

macro.risk: Australian/NZ household leverage and housing market
macro.description: High household debt-to-income levels in Australia/NZ leave mortgage books sensitive to unemployment shocks or house price declines
US tariff policy, US-China rivalry and supply-chain decoupling create volatility for ANZ's trade-finance and institutional Asia franchise
ANZ Research notes 2025 global growth (~3.2%) is the weakest since the pandemic-affected 2020, with below-trend growth in many advanced economies

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian and NZ banking is a mature, oligopolistic, heavily regulated industry; NZ Commerce Commission is pushing structural reforms (open banking, switching ease) to increase competition, while in Australia intense mortgage/deposit price competition continues; NZ industry revenue is forecast to decline as interest rates fall through 2025-26
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical - earnings sensitive to credit growth, net interest margin, and credit impairment charges through the economic cycle; less discretionary-consumer-exposed than retailers but exposed to housing and business credit cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - net interest margin, deposit/loan repricing dynamics, and the replicating portfolio/capital hedge all directly affected by RBA/RBNZ rate settings and yield curve shape
key_input_costs: Technology and platform investment (ANZ Plus, Suncorp migration)
Personnel costs and regulatory/compliance remediation spend

recent_developments.event: H1-2026 results: statutory profit flat YoY at $3,650m, cash profit up 6% to $3,780m; cash ROTE up 161bps to 11.6%; CET1 ratio 12.4%; interim dividend held at 83 cents per share with franking raised to 75%; remaining ~$800m of on-market buyback ceased
Suncorp Bank customer migration program 34% complete against the accelerated June 2027 full-migration target; Suncorp customer base grown ~5% to ~1.3 million since acquisition announcement

FY2025 full-year results: statutory profit down $560m (-8.5%) to $6,035m; cash profit down 13% to $5,931m; cost-to-income ratio (cash) rose to 58.2% from 51.3% on Suncorp integration, restructuring, and one-off charges

ANZ 2030 Strategy Day: management (new CEO Nuno Matos and CFO Farhan Faruqui) announced acceleration of Suncorp Bank migration to June 2027 and ANZ Plus rollout to all 8 million retail customers by September 2027; upgraded FY2026 cost-reduction and productivity-savings guidance

ANZ submitted Root Cause Remediation Plan (RCRP) to APRA under the Court Enforceable Undertaking; announced ~3,500 planned employee departures and reduced contractor engagements as part of an operating-model reset; entered ASIC settlement (~$240m penalties plus costs) covering Markets and Retail conduct matters, later confirmed via Federal Court orders totalling ~$250m
Nuno Matos formally became CEO and Executive Director (12 May 2025), succeeding long-serving CEO Shayne Elliott (2016-2025)

ANZ confirmed the Court Enforceable Undertaking with APRA and released the Oliver Wyman independent report into non-financial risk management and risk culture; APRA subsequently increased ANZ's operational risk capital add-on to $1 billion

ANZ NZ home-loan market share fell to ~30% as Kiwibank and ASB gained share through calendar 2025; ANZ progressing Commerce Commission recommendations from the personal banking competition market study

guidance.as_of: H1-2026 Results (March 2026) and October 2025 Strategy Day

items.notes: Upgraded from an earlier ~3% reduction target off the FY2025 ~$11.85bn baseline (adjusted for significant items), reflecting faster productivity delivery
Up from prior $800 million target; plus an expected ~$210 million FX translation benefit if rates hold near H1-2026 average
Brought forward from original later timeline at the October 2025 Strategy Day; 34% complete as of March 2026; targeting ~$500m p.a. run-rate synergies

items.target: All ~8 million retail customers migrated to ANZ Plus platform
items.notes: Three years earlier than the original plan; ANZ Plus already >45% of new retail product sales

items.target: Maintain CET1 comfortably above regulatory minimum while absorbing APRA's $1bn operational risk capital add-on
items.notes: CET1 was 12.4% at March 2026, up from 12.0% at September 2025
Board prioritising capital build and remediation funding over further buybacks in the near term; dividend held flat at 83 cents interim with franking increased to 75%

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Nuno Matos has framed FY2026-27 as a 'get the basics right' phase, with five immediate priorities: resetting culture, integrating Suncorp Bank, building a single customer front-end, driving deep productivity improvements, and remediating non-financial risk (NFR) matters. Management says the Root Cause Remediation Plan was approved by APRA in September 2025 and the PACT (People, Accountability, Customers, Trust) program is on track. CFO Farhan Faruqui highlighted improved capital position, higher collective provision coverage, and an improving dividend outlook, while flagging Markets income normalization and ongoing NIM competition as headwinds.

bull_case: New CEO-led cost/productivity reset is ahead of schedule (upgraded FY2026 savings guidance), with cost-to-income ratio set to improve materially from the FY2025 Suncorp/remediation-inflated 58.2% peak

Suncorp Bank acquisition makes ANZ the #3 Australian home lender with a credible path to ~$500m p.a. synergies once migration completes by June 2027, and accelerated ANZ Plus rollout could structurally lower the cost-to-serve

H1-2026 results already show the turn - cash profit up 6% YoY, cash ROTE up 161bps to 11.6%, CET1 strengthened to 12.4% - suggesting the FY2025 trough (one-off restructuring, ASIC settlement, PT Panin impairment) is largely behind the company
Diversified franchise across Australia, NZ, Pacific and Asia Institutional banking provides earnings resilience versus single-market peers, with a differentiated trade/Markets business
Attractive, well-covered dividend (83 cents interim, ~66-69% cash payout ratio) with potential for resumed buybacks once capital build and APRA remediation are further along
bear_case: APRA Court Enforceable Undertaking and ongoing Root Cause Remediation Plan represent multi-year execution risk and an unusually weak non-financial risk track record versus Big Four peers, with the $1bn capital add-on a permanent drag on returns until removed

Simultaneous, large-scale change programs (Suncorp migration, ANZ Plus rollout, cost-out, culture reset, new CEO) create meaningful execution risk of cost overruns, customer attrition or delivery slippage
Losing NZ mortgage market share to Kiwibank/ASB and facing structural competitive reform (Commerce Commission-driven open banking) could erode ANZ's historically strong New Zealand franchise

Net interest margin remains under pressure from deposit/loan pricing competition and wholesale funding costs, while credit impairment charges and impaired assets are rising off a benign base, pointing to potential cyclical credit normalization

Repeated conduct/regulatory failures (bond-trading misreporting, ASIC penalties, APRA CEU) have damaged trust and could recur, risking further fines, remediation costs or reputational share loss to challengers
